    First extensions between interval representations (4.1) #

    Since P i and Y are injective, Ext¹(-, P i) = Ext¹(-, Y) = 0. Applying Hom(B, -) to 0 → A i → P i → Y → 0 shows that every class in Ext¹(B, A i) is g^* ε_i for some g : B ⟶ Y, where ε_i is the class of the sequence, and g^* ε_i = 0 exactly when g factors through c_i : P i ⟶ Y. With table (2.2) this gives the only nonzero first extension spaces between intervals: Ext¹(Y, A i) ≃ k and Ext¹(P j, A i) ≃ k for j < i.
